ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-intensity (light gray/white) background with a large, centralized low-intensity (black) region. Ratio of light to dark pixels is approximately 3:1.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Centralized, dark 'butterfly' shaped pigmentation region radiating from the notch. Multiple discrete, high-contrast dark circular blobs (rosettes) clustered on the distal and medial left lobe. Sparse dark spots on the distal right lobe. Dark edging along the entire trailing margin.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, symmetrical V-shaped notch. The inner angle is sharp, with a vertical depth of approximately 1/8th of the visible fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous irregular serrations along the trailing edge. High-frequency peaks and valleys, particularly prominent on the distal portions of both lobes. The edge appears jagged rather than smooth.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave trailing edge curve. The lobes sweep upwards and outwards towards pointed distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Densely packed cluster of approximately 12-15 dark circular spots on the distal left lobe. A secondary cluster of 6-8 spots is located on the mid-left lobe near the dark central pigmentation border. Scattered individual spots are visible on the right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several faint, unaligned dark horizontal streaks visible on the medial-right lobe, traversing the light-pigmented surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive focal scarring (rosettes) likely from previous barnacle colonization, heavily concentrated on the left lobe. Deep pigmentation pattern at the center.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique spatial distribution of high-contrast rosettes on the left lobe contrasting with the relatively clear right lobe and the large central dark pigmentation zone.
